title: Adaptable top_k contract and 'hop' pagination for rerank endpoint
creator: Ava Patel
description: Goal: Redesign the rerank endpoint contract to support flexible top_k semantics (absolute k, fraction-of-candidates, score-threshold modes), provide a lightweight "hop" pagination alternative to large offset/continuation burdens, and produce a consistent structured output that includes provenance and score breakdowns. This ticket covers API surface, server semantics, migration strategy and a staged rollout focused on quality, latency, and operational scalability.
background: Current rerank endpoint only accepts an integer top_k and returns a single page containing the top-N results or a continuation token designed around a strict cursor. Customers and internal teams have asked for: (1) more expressive top_k semantics to cover use cases like return top X% of candidates or only items above a score threshold; (2) an ergonomic pagination primitive for iterative scanning without heavy server-side state or expensive offset scans; (3) richer per-item metadata for explainability (feature-level scores, embedding similarity, provenance references) while keeping token/CPU cost low. Past tickets (ENG-59873, ENG-31122) attempted related ergonomics but left gaps in semantics clarity and migration paths.
proposed_solution: 1) top_k parameter becomes a union-style contract encoded as an object: {mode: 'absolute'|'fraction'|'threshold', value: number}. - absolute: value=integer N. - fraction: value=0.0-1.0 interpreted as fraction of input candidates to return (ceil), with a configurable cap. - threshold: value=score cutoff in normalized score space. 2) Introduce 'hop' pagination: client supplies {anchor: optional result_id, hop_size: integer}. Server returns up to hop_size items after the anchor in stable rank order and an optional next_anchor value. Hops are cheap to compute because servers use precalculated partial top-k sketches rather than scanning offsets. 3) Structured output envelope: items array where each item includes id, short_text, score, explain: [ {component: 'embedding_sim', weight: 0.74}, {component: 'rule_boost', weight: 0.08} ], provenance: [uri|doc_id references], and a compact 'trace' token for debugging. 4) Stability rules: deterministic tie-breaking using stable candidate id ordering and explicit 'mode' semantics for inclusive/exclusive behavior. 5) Performance: allow server to short-circuit when threshold mode produces fewer results; add support for batched rerank across multiple request groups to improve throughput; streaming hop responses for low-latency first-results. 6) Backward compatibility: default top_k requests without the new object continue to operate as before (absolute mode).
acceptance_criteria:
1) API accepts top_k as new object and supports absolute/fraction/threshold modes; legacy integer top_k is still accepted as absolute mode.
2) Hop pagination returns stable, deterministic next_anchor and supports hop_size up to configured cap (default 100).
3) Response includes explain[] and provenance[] fields for each item when request asks for explain=true; these fields are compact by default.
4) Server-side benchmarks show <=5% median latency regression for absolute mode; fraction/threshold/hop modes show no worse than 20% regression and yield improved tail for streaming first-hop.
5) Comprehensive unit + integration tests exist and pass in CI; e2e load tests show expected throughput with batched rerank.
6) Migration docs published and SDKs updated with examples; opt-in rollout completed before deprecation of legacy continuation behavior.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement server support and add 'top_k' object parsing while keeping legacy integer behavior; expose hop pagination as opt-in via query param 'pagination=hop'. Phase 2 (SDK release): update SDKs and publish docs + migration guide with examples and recommended patterns. Phase 3 (wider rollout): enable hop pagination for 25% of traffic; collect metrics and customer feedback. Phase 4 (deprecation): announce deprecation window for non-stable continuation offsets (if any), provide automated converter in SDKs and a compatibility flag for 90 days.
implementation_plan: A) Api/parsing layer (Diego) - add top_k object parsing, input validation and schema docs. B) Server selection logic (Infra team) - implement fraction/threshold handling and cap enforcement. C) Hop pagination engine (Serving runtime) - add lightweight sketch-based anchor hops and streaming response. D) Explainability payload (Research/Product) - standardize minimal explain components to keep size small. E) SDK and docs (DX) - examples, migration helpers, and tests. F) Perf tuning and benchmarks (SRE/Benchmarking). Expected timeline: 3 sprints with cross-team checkpoints.
test_plan:
- Unit tests: parser, validator, deterministic tie-breaker.
- Integration: full request->response validation including explain/provenance flags.
- Perf: compare absolute baseline vs new modes for median/tail p50/p95 under representative workloads.
- Chaos: simulate partial index/unavailable candidates and verify hop anchor correctness.
- Compatibility: run existing customers' test suites against canary to detect regressions.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood release to platform teams. 2) Canary: 3% of production traffic with telemetry for latency, correctness, and bundle size. 3) Gradual increase to 25% and then 100% if SLAs hold. 4) Post-mortem and rollback plan prepared; toggle via runtime feature flag.
